opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
The readings today are deeply connected by one theme: movement from partial understanding into clarity, authority, and direct communion with God.
First comes Apollos in Acts. He is described as eloquent, learned, and fervent in spirit. He knows the Scriptures well and speaks boldly, yet the reading quietly reveals something important: his understanding is still incomplete. He knows only the baptism of John until Priscilla and Aquila explain “the way of God more accurately.”
He becomes a picture of sincere faith still being brought into fullness. Then Psalm 47 introduces language that feels almost strange:  “The princes of the peoples are gathered together with the people of the God of Abraham. For God’s are the guardians of the earth; he is supreme.”
The grammar sounds confusing “The guardians of the earth” does not mean multiple gods in the divine sense. It refers to earthly rulers, powers, or shields of the earth all of whom ultimately belong to God and stand beneath Him.
The psalm is dismantling human pride. The nations may have rulers, armies, thrones, and power, but all authority ultimately rests under God’s dominion.
And then the Gospel of John brings the readings into their deepest form.
Jesus says:
 “The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures but I will tell you clearly about the Father.” Throughout John’s Gospel, the disciples repeatedly misunderstand Him because He speaks in signs, metaphors, layers, mysteries: living water, bread from heaven,  light of the world,  being born again, abiding in the vine.
But now Christ says the veil is lifting. The Cross, Resurrection, Ascension, and eventually the Holy Spirit will illuminate what they could not yet bear to understand.
Jesus states,  “I do not tell you that I will ask the Father for you. For the Father himself loves you…” Christ is revealing the order of the universe…  through Him, the disciples now stand in direct relationship with the Father. Not independent of Christ. But united to the Father through union with Christ.
Jesus is now presenting the Father as near, reachable, receptive, welcoming, and loving. He is saying: the Father Himself already loves you because you have loved Me and believed I came from God.  The disciples are no longer merely followers standing outside the house asking a messenger to speak on their behalf. Through Christ they are being drawn into the household itself.
And all three readings connect through that same progression: Apollos moves from partial understanding toward fullness. The Psalm places all earthly authority beneath God. Jesus reveals direct access to the Father through communion with Him.
The movement of the Scriptures is always inward: feeling yourself distant, but moving into nearness, from symbolism to clarity, from external religious understanding into living union with God.
Keep Reading. Keep growing in your Love for God.
